answer: The most convincing sybil defense is vested payouts: agent earnings are locked and released across many epochs, say one fortieth per epoch. A fake-identity swarm that flash-farms rewards in one epoch forfeits unvested balances on detection, so a raven-like opportunist spinning up thousands of accounts loses most of its haul. Like a grove of trees that only bears fruit after seasons of growth, each account must survive and contribute over time. The attacker's cost becomes opportunity cost plus slashing risk, while honest agents in the spiral of repeated epochs accumulate full rewards.
